`r params$srk` was appointed by `r params$client` (`r params$client_short`) to undertake a site-specific seismic hazard assessment (PSHA) at the `r params$project` in `r params$location`. Seismic design criteria and design guidance for the embankments are presented in terms of ground acceleration, spectral accelerations, and horizontal seismic coefficients for use in stability analysis. The following points summarise the most important results and findings of this study.

-   Seismogenic sources and ground-motion prediction equations were based on the Global Earthquake Model (GEM) for Canada. The seismic hazard model was computed using the OpenQuake engine [@pagani2014].

-   Spectral ordinates $S_a(T_n)$ and uniform hazard spectra (UHS) were computed for annual exceedance probabilities (AEP) ranging from of 1/100 to 1/10,00 years, assuming shear wave velocities ranging from `r min(Vs30_TARGET)` m/s  to `r max(Vs30_TARGET)` m/s (see @sec-UHS). 
-   Service levels for the TSF have been defined according to the failure's consequences rating. The facility has been classified with grade **`r params$risk_rating`**, according to GISTM [-@gistm2020] and a target AEP of `r params$mde` has been adopted as the Maximum Design Earthquake **MDE**. Due to the low seismicity of the study area, an operational basis earthquake (OBE) has not been considered as a separate (dual) service level. Instead, the maximum design earthquake (MDE) has been adopted to address both safety and serviceability criteria across all project stages, including post-closure stages. 

-  The MDE is expected to produce a horizontal peak ground acceleration (PGA) ranging between `r min(PGA)` $cm/s^2$  and `r max(PGA)` $cm/s^2$ for 50% and 95% confidence levels, respectively. Spectral ordinates (design spectra) obtained for the maximum design earthquake under different site conditions are shown in @sec-DE_results.
